$comment: Authoritative schema for /var/www/instrumetriq-api/data/extension_payload.json. Generated from scripts/build_payload.py and cross-checked against EXTENSION_PLAN.md. The source of truth for archive field semantics is /srv/cryptobot/ARCHIVE_ENTRY_FULL_SCHEMA.json.
title: Instrumetriq Extension Payload
description: Static JSON file written atomically by build_payload.py on the VPS every ~10 minutes (cron every 10 min, but only rebuilds when update_csvs.py has finished a newer cycle). Consumed by the extension's background service worker via a bearer-token-authenticated fetch. The file contains one entry per coin in the 257-coin universe, regardless of data quality - consumers must check 'ok' flags before using any sub-block.

pushed_at.description: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp of when this payload was written by build_payload.py. Format: 'YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ'. The extension service worker compares this to the previously cached pushed_at to detect a new cycle and decide whether to fire notifications or refresh the popup.

feed_ok.description: False if the most recent archive timestamp across all coins is older than 6 hours (FEED_INTERRUPTED_H = 6). Indicates the upstream scraper pipeline has stalled. When false, the extension badge turns amber (#FFB74D) regardless of badge mode, and the popup shows a feed-interrupted warning. True does not guarantee all coins are fresh - it only means at least one coin has a recent data point.

active_coin_count.description: Count of coins currently at 'Buzzing' or 'Spiking' chatter level across the entire universe. Used in two places: (1) the popup footer CTA ('N coins are Buzzing or Spiking right now'), (2) badge 'all_coins' mode - the badge turns cyan when this count is > 0. A coin is counted only if chatter.ok is true and chatter.level is 'Buzzing' or 'Spiking'.

coins.description: Array of per-coin objects, one entry per symbol in coin_universe.json (257 coins). Sorted alphabetically by symbol. Every coin in the universe always has an entry - consumers must check ok flags before using sub-blocks. coins with no CSV data at all will have chatter.ok=false, futures.ok=false, volume.ok=false, quality='insufficient_data'.

CoinEntry.description: All data for one coin. Sub-blocks (chatter, futures, volume) each carry an 'ok' boolean. Never render a sub-block's data unless its ok is true.

symbol.description: Canonical uppercase ticker symbol as used by the scraper and coin_universe.json. Examples: 'BTC', 'ETH', 'DOGE'. This is the primary key used by the popup to match coins in the user's tracked list.

pair_symbols.description: All known trading pair strings for this coin, sourced from coin_universe.json (which is originally derived from /srv/twscrape/config/twitter_coin_synonyms.json). Includes the base symbol itself plus USDT/USDC/BTC-quoted pairs, e.g. ['ZEN', 'ZENUSDC', 'ZENUSDT', 'ZENBTC']. Used by content.js for URL symbol resolution: the content script compares the extracted pair string from the exchange URL against this array to identify the coin.

chatter.description: X (Twitter) chatter metrics for this coin. Always present. Check 'ok' before using any other field.

futures.description: Perpetual futures metrics for this coin. Always present. Check 'ok' before using any other field.

volume.description: 24-hour Binance spot trading volume for this coin. Present when CSV data exists. Absent entirely if no rows were found in the CSV. Check 'ok' before using any other field.

sparkline.description: Variable-length array of raw Engagement Coefficient (EC) values, one per archive cycle processed, oldest first. EC formula: (total_likes + total_retweets) * log1p(followers_sum) / posts_total. Values range from 0.0 (silent cycle - scraper ran but found zero posts) to 100,000+ for viral spikes. Zeros are real data points, not missing data. Null entries appear when is_silent=true for a cycle or when raw data was insufficient to compute EC. Array length varies per coin (up to ~420 entries for a coin with 30 days of history at ~2h cadence). Absent entirely if no CSV/history exists. The popup renders only the most recent 7 days ('cycle' mode default). EC is also used to compute the chatter level and the 30-day rolling mean baseline.

sparkline_tone.description: Array of tone shift integers, element-aligned with 'sparkline', oldest first. Each value is the shift for that cycle: (pos_ratio - neg_ratio - baseline) * 100, rounded and clamped to -100..100. Null when the cycle fails the tone quality gate (posts_total < 5, twitter_data_ok=false, primary_conf_mean < 0.55) or when fewer than 30 qualifying cycles exist to establish a baseline. The popup maps each integer directly to a bar color: shift > +8 -> green (--tone-positive, CSS class 'positive'), shift < -8 -> red (--tone-negative, class 'negative'), -8 to +8 or null -> grey (--tone-mixed, class 'mixed'). Note: the EXTENSION_PLAN.md shows this array as strings ('Positive', 'Mixed', 'Negative') - that is an illustrative example only. The actual payload always contains integers (or null).

sparkline_pos.description: Array of pos_ratio values (0.0..1.0), element-aligned with 'sparkline', oldest first. pos_ratio is the fraction of posts scored as positive sentiment by the NLP classifier. Null for cycles that fail the tone quality gate. Used by the popup's day/week aggregated sparkline modes to compute average positivity per bucket.

sparkline_neg.description: Array of neg_ratio values (0.0..1.0), element-aligned with 'sparkline', oldest first. neg_ratio is the fraction of posts scored as negative sentiment by the NLP classifier. Null for cycles that fail the tone quality gate. Used alongside sparkline_pos by the day/week aggregation logic.

sparkline_ts.description: Array of ISO 8601 UTC timestamps, element-aligned with 'sparkline', oldest first. Format: 'YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MMZ' (no seconds). Derived from the 'ts' column of the per-coin CSV, which in turn maps to the archive file's hour bucket. Used by the popup to: (1) enforce a rolling 7-day window cutoff for cycle mode, (2) derive x-axis labels (first and last visible timestamps), (3) aggregate entries into daily or weekly buckets in day/week modes.

quality.description: Summary quality flag for this coin entry. 'ok' if at least one of chatter.ok or futures.ok is true (the coin has some usable data). 'insufficient_data' if both chatter and futures are unavailable. The popup may use this to render a minimal 'no data yet' placeholder instead of a full card. Note: the EXTENSION_PLAN.md also lists 'uncertain', 'stale', 'no_futures' as possible future values, but as of the current build_payload.py implementation only 'ok' and 'insufficient_data' are written.

ChatterOk.description: Chatter block when sufficient data exists to compute an EC-based level. ok is always true in this variant.

ok.description: Always true in this variant. Indicates that a current EC value and 30-day mean were both computable.

level.description: Chatter level derived from the ratio of the current cycle's EC to the coin's 30-day rolling mean EC. Thresholds: < 0.5x mean = 'Quiet', 0.5-2x = 'Active', 2-6x = 'Buzzing', > 6x = 'Spiking'. When the mean is 0 (coin has had no engagement in 30 days), level is always 'Quiet'. 'Buzzing' and 'Spiking' trigger badge updates and notifications.

tone_shift.description: The tone shift for the most recent cycle: (pos_ratio - neg_ratio - baseline) * 100, rounded and clamped to -100..100. Positive = current sentiment is more positive than this coin's usual level. Negative = more negative than usual. Null when the most recent cycle fails the tone quality gate (posts_total < 5, primary_conf_mean < 0.55, twitter_data_ok=false) or when fewer than 30 qualifying historical cycles exist to establish a baseline. This is a relative metric - it measures deviation from this coin's own history, not an absolute positivity score.

tone_raw.description: The raw net sentiment score for the most recent cycle: (pos_ratio - neg_ratio) * 100, rounded and clamped to -100..100. Unlike tone_shift, this is an absolute score independent of the coin's historical baseline. Null when the cycle fails the tone quality gate. Displayed alongside tone_shift in the popup detail panel for context.

tone_baseline.description: The coin's 30-day mean net sentiment score: mean(pos_ratio - neg_ratio) * 100 across all qualifying historical cycles, rounded. Null when fewer than 30 qualifying cycles exist. Displayed in the popup tooltip as context for the shift: 'This coin's 30-day baseline is X. Current sentiment has shifted Y points above/below its usual level.'

tone_pos.description: The positive sentiment ratio for the most recent cycle, as an integer percentage: pos_ratio * 100, rounded. Null when the cycle fails the tone quality gate. pos_ratio is the fraction of NLP-scored posts classified as positive. Together with tone_neg, gives an absolute breakdown of sentiment (vs the shift-based tone_shift which is relative to history).

tone_neg.description: The negative sentiment ratio for the most recent cycle, as an integer percentage: neg_ratio * 100, rounded. Null when the cycle fails the tone quality gate. neg_ratio is the fraction of NLP-scored posts classified as negative.

updated_ago_min.description: Minutes since the last data row's archive timestamp, computed at payload build time. Derived from (build_time - last_ts) in seconds / 60. Null if the timestamp could not be parsed. Displayed in the popup card header as 'Updated Xm ago'. Because the payload is cached by the extension until the next fetch cycle, the actual staleness the user sees is updated_ago_min + (minutes since the extension last fetched). It does NOT reflect when build_payload.py ran - it reflects when the upstream scraper last deposited an archive file with data for this coin.

distinct_authors.description: Number of distinct Twitter/X user accounts whose posts were collected and attributed to this coin in the most recent scraper cycle. Sourced from the 'distinct_authors' field of the archive entry. A higher number indicates broader organic participation rather than a single account driving engagement. Shown in the popup detail panel as a secondary context metric alongside the chatter level.

ChatterFailed.description: Chatter block when EC could not be computed (no CSV data, EC came out null, or mean is 0 with no current EC). The popup must hide the chatter section for this coin.

FuturesOk.description: Futures block when all four gate conditions pass: futures_contract_exists=true, futures_data_ok=true, futures_stale=false, futures_age_sec <= 3600.

funding_label.description: Human-readable label for the current 8-hour perpetual funding rate direction. 'Longs paying' when funding_now > 0 (longs pay shorts, indicating net bullish bias in the market). 'Shorts paying' when funding_now < 0 (shorts pay longs, indicating net bearish bias). 'Neutral' when exactly 0. Sourced from futures_raw.funding_now in the archive. Per wording rules, never use 'bullish'/'bearish' - only these exact label strings.

funding_rate.description: Formatted absolute value of the 8-hour funding rate as a percentage string with 4 decimal places. Format: '{value}%'. Example: '0.0100%' means the funding rate is 0.01% per 8 hours (= 0.03% per day). The popup appends ' / 8h' when displaying this value. Always the absolute value - direction is conveyed by funding_label.

oi_label.description: Change in open interest since the previous cycle. 'OI rising' when oi_delta_pct > 0.005 (more than +0.5% change). 'OI falling' when oi_delta_pct < -0.005 (more than -0.5% change). 'OI stable' within the -0.5% to +0.5% band. oi_delta_pct is a decimal fraction from the archive (e.g. 0.074 = +7.4%). Rising OI with elevated funding may indicate a crowded trade.

oi_usd.description: Raw total open interest in USD, rounded to 2 decimal places. Sourced from the archive's open_interest field (which stores the USD value from Binance /fapi/v1/ticker/openInterest combined with the mark price). Used by the popup when a precise number is needed (e.g. tooltip). For display, use oi_usd_fmt instead.

oi_usd_fmt.description: Human-readable formatted open interest. Formatted by build_payload.py's format_usd() function: >= $1B -> '$X.XB', >= $1M -> '$X.XM', >= $1K -> '$X.XK', else '$X'. Example: '$1.2B', '$345.6M', '$78.9K'. Used directly in the popup card's OI row value display.

whale_label.description: Derived from the whale_ratio field (large-account long/short ratio from Binance's /futures/data/topLongShortAccountRatio endpoint). The thresholds are market-wide percentiles recomputed each build cycle across all coins that pass the futures gate. 'Whales leaning long' when this coin's whale_ratio > the market's 75th-percentile ratio (p75). 'Whales leaning short' when < p25. 'Neutral' otherwise. Using market-relative thresholds (rather than a fixed value like 1.0) normalises for the fact that market-wide positioning drifts with macro conditions.

whale_pct.description: The long-side percentage of large-account positioning, derived from whale_ratio. Formula: round(whale_ratio / (1 + whale_ratio) * 100). A whale_ratio of 1.5 -> 60% longs. Shown in the popup as a supplementary number alongside the whale_label, e.g. '60% long'. When whale_ratio is 0 or negative (data anomaly), defaults to 50.

whale_ratio.description: Raw long/short ratio for large accounts (whale_ratio), rounded to 4 decimal places. Sourced from Binance /futures/data/topLongShortAccountRatio. A value > 1.0 means more large accounts are net long than short. Value < 1.0 means more are net short. The market-wide p25 and p75 at build time determine the whale_label bands. Included for clients that want to inspect the raw value rather than rely on the label.

FuturesFailed.description: Futures block when any gate condition fails. The popup must hide the entire futures section for this coin - never show a partial futures card.

reason.description: Machine-readable reason for the gate failure. 'no_contract' = futures_contract_exists is false (coin has no listed perpetual). 'data_error' = futures_data_ok is false (scraper encountered an error fetching futures data). 'stale' = futures_stale flag is true OR futures_age_sec > 3600 (data is older than 1 hour). 'no_data' = no CSV rows were found for this coin at all. Not displayed to the user - used for internal debugging and metrics.

VolumeOk.description: Volume block when at least one volume_usd data point exists in the coin's CSV history.

usd.description: Raw 24-hour trading volume in USD for the most recent cycle, rounded to 2 decimal places. Sourced from the archive's spot_raw.liq_qv_usd field (Binance /api/v3/ticker/24hr quoteVolume). This is a rolling 24-hour window, not a within-cycle delta. Used to compute the percentile ranking against this coin's own historical distribution.

usd_fmt.description: Human-readable formatted 24-hour volume using the same format_usd() function as oi_usd_fmt. Displayed in the popup card's volume row.

label.description: Volume level relative to this coin's own historical distribution (not market-wide). Derived from the percentile rank of the current volume across all historical volume_usd values in this coin's 30-day CSV. Thresholds: > 75th percentile = 'Elevated', > 50th = 'Above avg', >= 25th = 'Below avg', < 25th = 'Low'. This is always a self-relative comparison - a coin that is consistently low-volume will never show 'Elevated' just because it had one above-average day.

pct.description: Exact percentile rank of the current volume_usd within this coin's own historical distribution, rounded to 1 decimal place. Computed using a midpoint ranking formula: (count_below + 0.5 * count_equal) / total * 100. Included for clients that want more precision than the four-bucket label provides.

VolumeFailed.description: Volume block when no volume_usd values exist in the coin's CSV history.
